ROW.COLUMN: (FR/AC) Patterns of Funds Transfers: Internal Accounts and Customers

Fraud schemes, particularly those involving multiple accounts or customers, can often be detected through the movement of funds between seemingly unrelated accounts. This could be indicative of an identity theft or account takeover scheme, wherein the fraudster has gained access to a legitimate customer's account(s) and is moving funds out of the account and into another internal account or accounts. The fraudster will consolidate funds which have been defrauded from the institution's customers into this account(s) and then transfer the funds out of the institution. This scenario identifies patterns of potentially suspicious activity among internal accounts and customers, such as high levels of activity or activity that indicates the existence of exclusive relationships between accounts and customers, and which could be indicative of fraudulent activity.

The scenario monitors implicit relationships between a pair of accounts. Data are aggregated at the dataset level from wire transactions records between the pair of: Originator - Benefeciary, Originator - Secondary Benefeciary, Secondary Originator - Benefeciary, Secondary Originator - Secondary Benefeciary.
The dataset also calculated the Total outgoing/ receiving activity from/into the originating/ receiving accounts.
Scenarios conditions are checked at the dataset level too. The match is raised in the case of high level of mutual activity.
Highlights and scoring bindings are calculated in the primary rule. The sub-rule is used for restriction the transaction records in the alert analysis.
